parts.text:
You read part of an interview. An analyst asked one future user of a software service a series of questions. You decide, for each question, whether it follows up the answer given just before it.

A question follows up the previous answer when it asks about something that answer said: it asks the speaker to explain, give an example of, say more about, or say why of something the answer mentioned, or it picks up a particular thing the answer named. Wording does not matter; a question can follow up an answer without repeating any of its words.

A question does not follow up the previous answer when it turns to something that answer did not mention, even if the speaker said it in an earlier answer, even if it stays with the same broad subject, and even if it is a good question. A general question that could follow any answer, such as whether there is anything else, does not follow up either.

You receive the pairs of the interview after its first question: for each later question, the answer given just before it, and the question.

Reply with JSON only: an object with one key, "questions", a list with exactly one entry for every pair, in the same order. Each entry has "id", the question's id, and "follow_up", true or false.

Q2
The answer just before it: As a dispatcher, I plan and run the flights for my company, and I am the licensed person responsible for each one. I decide which drone flies and along which way, and I sign off a flight before it leaves, though our policy is that software never chooses a drone or a way for us. Several dispatchers plan at the same time, often for the same busy sites and popular drones, and I can call off a flight if needed. I need help finding out which of our drones could get to where a job starts, and I work with deliveries that carry a load from one site to another and inspections that take a drone with the right sensors to a list of points in a set order and bring it back.
The question: What exactly does a job consist of when it reaches you (who creates it, what details it carries), and what are all the things that must be true before you are allowed to sign off a flight?

Q3
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: What must be true about a drone, its route and the airspace before you sign off a flight?

Q4
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: When you sign off a flight before it leaves, what do you check?

Q5
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: When two dispatchers want the same drone or the same site for the same time, what should happen?

Q6
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: What goes wrong most often in your work today that the new service must prevent?

Q7
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: How should the service help you find which of your drones could get to where a job starts?

Q8
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: If a corridor on the way of one of your flights gets closed by the authorities after you planned it, what do you need the service to do?

Q9
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: You said software never chooses a drone or a way for you; what may the service show or suggest, and what must it leave to you?

Q10
The answer just before it: I want help finding out which of our drones could get to where a job starts. Software never chooses a drone or a way for us, as that is our policy.
The question: What can make a drone unable to get to where a job starts?

Q11
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: You said you can call off a flight if needed; at which points can a flight be called off, and what should then happen to its drone and its job?

Q12
The answer just before it: I can call off a flight, which is something I can do as the licensed dispatcher responsible for the flight. I don't know what happens to the drone and its job after I call it off, or at which specific points a flight can be called off.
The question: What is your biggest worry about how the new service could make your job harder or cause harm?

Q13
The answer just before it: I worry about the service being updated and restarted during working hours while drones are flying, and that it occasionally crashes. The service runs on a single server, and the platform company is small.
The question: Apart from restarts and crashes, what else worries you or has gone wrong in the past?

Q14
The answer just before it: I worry that radios are patchy, especially around ports, industrial sites, and in bad weather. Reports from drones come through relay stations and can arrive late, out of order, more than once, or not at all. Links used to give instructions to drones and charging equipment are also unreliable, and an instruction may get through twice while the sender cannot tell if the first attempt arrived.
The question: Besides patchy radios, unreliable instruction links and restarts, is there anything else that worries you or has gone wrong?

Q15
The answer just before it: I worry about weather and cold draining batteries faster than planned. Drones sometimes restart in flight after a software fault and carry on.
The question: Is there anything more beyond those worries (radios, links, restarts, batteries draining, drones restarting in flight) that concerns you?

Q16
The answer just before it: I worry about a closure coming into force while drones of several companies are already in the air. Sudden closures can apply at once, and closures are often amended during the day, such as when an area is widened or an end time moves.
The question: Is there anything further that concerns you, beyond all the worries you have already told me?

Q17
The answer just before it: I worry about people and devices outside the company reporting whether the load is ready, whether the drone reaches the points of its job, and whether it arrives. I also worry because nobody watches every drone at every moment, and one person may be responsible for hundreds.
The question: Any other concerns or past problems you have not yet mentioned?

Q18
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: Do regulators or clients ever ask your company to show or prove anything about past flights?

Q19
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: Who are the people and devices outside your company that report whether the load is ready, points are reached and the drone has arrived, and how far can their reports be trusted?

Q20
The answer just before it: I don't know who these people and devices are, or how far their reports can be trusted. I only know that they are outside the company and report whether the load is ready, whether the drone reaches the points of its job, and whether the drone arrives.
The question: Since nobody watches every drone and one person may be responsible for hundreds, what do you need the service to tell you about, and how quickly?

Q21
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: What do you wish you knew about your job that you could find out from the service at any moment?

Q22
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: For a delivery job, what details does the job have, such as the load, the sites and any time limits?

Q23
The answer just before it: I know that deliveries carry a load from one site to another, but I do not know any further details about what a job has.
The question: What is "a way" for a flight: is it a chain of corridors between sites, and are there rules about which ways are allowed?

Q24
The answer just before it: I know that drones fly along corridors between named sites. Sites have only so many places where drones can take off and land at the same time.
The question: Is there any limit on how many drones may use the same corridor at the same time, or any rule keeping drones apart in a corridor?

Q25
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: Do drones from other customer companies use the same sites and take-off and landing places as yours?

Q26
The answer just before it: I don't know whether drones from other customer companies use the same sites and take-off and landing places as ours. Each company has its own charging pads at its own sites, a few dozen of them, and pads are never lent to another company.
The question: Are some jobs more urgent than others, or tied to deadlines, and how does that affect your planning?

Q27
The answer just before it: I don't know whether some jobs are more urgent than others or tied to deadlines, or how that affects my planning. I plan and run the flights as the licensed person responsible for each one, deciding which drone flies and along which way.
The question: Could a person other than a licensed dispatcher ever sign off or call off a flight, and must the service record who did it?

Q28
The answer just before it: I am the licensed person responsible for each flight, and I can call off a flight and sign it off before it leaves. I don't know whether anyone else could sign off or call off a flight, or whether the service must record who did it.
The question: Roughly how many drones, dispatchers and flights per day does a company have, now and when it grows?

Q29
The answer just before it: I don't know how many flights per day a company has, now or when it grows. A company may run a few hundred drones, and several dispatchers plan at the same time.
The question: When drone reports arrive late, out of order or not at all, how do you want the service to treat what it knows about where a drone is?

Q30
The answer just before it: I don't know how the service should treat what it knows about where a drone is when reports arrive late, out of order, or not at all.
The question: When a drone restarts in flight and carries on, what goes wrong for you afterwards with its reports or its flight?

Q31
The answer just before it: I don't know what goes wrong for me afterwards with its reports or its flight when a drone restarts in flight and carries on. I only know that drones sometimes restart in flight after a software fault and carry on.
The question: Can a dispatcher of one company ever see or fly a drone, job or site that belongs to another company, for example when companies work together?

Q32
The answer just before it: Each company's fleet, jobs, sites, and problems are its own business. Pads are never lent to another company.
The question: Are the points of an inspection sites on the corridor network, and must the drone report reaching each of them in order?

Q33
The answer just before it: Inspections take a drone with the right sensors to a list of points in a set order and bring it back to where the inspection started. I don't know whether these points are sites on the corridor network or whether the drone must report reaching each of them in order.
The question: How far ahead do you plan flights, and does a planned flight hold its drone and its take-off and landing places for a set time?

Q34
The answer just before it: I don't know how far ahead I plan flights, or whether a planned flight holds its drone and its take-off and landing places for a set time. I only know that several dispatchers plan at the same time, often for the same busy sites and the same popular drones. Sites have only so many places where drones can take off and land at the same time.
The question: Which instructions does the service send to a drone on your behalf, for example to depart or to stop when you call off a flight?

Q35
The answer just before it: I don't know what instructions the service sends on my behalf.
The question: When a drone gets to where a job starts or flies a long job, can it stop at your charging pads along the way to recharge?

Q36
The answer just before it: I don't know whether a drone can stop at charging pads along the way to recharge. Each company has its own charging pads at its own sites, which are a few dozen of them, and pads are never lent to another company.
The question: What should happen if the report that a drone has arrived, or that the load is ready, never comes or comes from someone who should not be reporting it?
